title: Adab with neighbors
hookLine: an oath said three times, a pot of soup with extra water, and the people on the other side of the wall

lines: SAID ONCE. AGAIN. A THIRD TIME.
THE ONE WHOSE NEIGHBOR ISN'T SAFE.
cards: By Allah, he does not believe. In paraphrase, those are the words, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said it once. Then again.
Then a third time. Someone asked: who? In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, his answer was: the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm.
Not a thief. Not a heretic. Someone living next door, whose neighbor has to stay a little on guard.

teach.b: Start with how high the Qur'an places the neighbor.

In surah al-Nisa, verse thirty-six, in paraphrase, the command to worship Allah alone runs straight into a list of people owed kindness: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is kin, the neighbor who is a stranger, and the companion at your side.
Worship and the house next door, in one breath.
Then 'A'ishah's report, in Bukhari, in paraphrase: Gabriel kept urging me to be good to the neighbor, until I thought he would make the neighbor an heir.
Then the oath from the hook, and what it asks: safety before generosity.
The first thing a neighbor is owed is the absence of harm: no noise flung over the fence, no gossip, no dread when your door opens. Only then the giving, and the giving is small on purpose.
In Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase, the Prophet told Abu Dharr: when you cook a broth, add more water, and look to your neighbors. A thinner soup, so it stretches one more house.
And in Bukhari, in paraphrase, he told the women of the community: let no neighbor look down on a gift to her neighbor, even a sheep's hoof. So the adab comes in two steps.
First, be someone the people beside you never have to brace for. Then, every so often, send something over.
This week the manners of daily life have walked outward: the journey, the pillow, the teacher, the road, the market, your mother, and now the people closest to your walls.

how: In Islamic teaching, kindness to neighbors is tied to faith, drawing on Qur'an 4:36 and hadith about keeping neighbors safe from harm and sharing food and small gifts with them.

o: the rules for settling property lines with the house next door
the manners owed to people next door: no harm, then small gifts
keeping to yourself so you never bother the people next door

games.q: adab with neighbors — tap the pairs.
p: a gift not to look down on

s: the hadith puts generosity before safety
the oath is about the one whose neighbor is not safe from his harm: safety comes first.
al-Nisa names the neighbor in the same verse as worship
verse 36 runs from worshipping Allah alone to kindness to the neighbor, kin and stranger.
a gift to a neighbor must be large to count
let no neighbor look down on a gift, even a sheep's hoof.

games.q: you're Abu Dharr, cooking a broth with not much in the pot. the Prophet gives you one instruction about it. what is it?
o: eat it yourself; charity starts at home.
add more water, and look to your neighbors.
save it for a guest of honor.
games.why: a thinner soup, so it reaches one more house (Sahih Muslim).

practice: Bring to mind the people closest to where you live: through the wall, across the hall, down the road, some known by name, some only by their car or their light at night. For each, ask quietly: is this person safe beside me?
Then pick one and picture a knock, or a word on the stairs; if you pray, hold that neighbor in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Adab with neighbors. The manners owed to the people beside you: first, safety from your harm; then, a little more water in the pot. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: safe beside you. Safety comes first, and then the soup. Tomorrow, adab with children.
